At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt
 On The 4 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 54512 of 2025
JAVITH AKTHAR @JAVITH S  Versus
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
Appearance:
Shri Mohd. Ali, learned Senior counsel with Shri Shar  Farooqui, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri G.S. Baghel, learned Government Advocate for
the  respondent/State.

ORDER This is fifth application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.314/2024 registered at Police Station-Gorakhpur, District- Jabalpur (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 409 & 120-B of IPC.

Applicant's first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 24.01.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.2496/2025, second application was dismissed on 10.03.2025 in M.Cr.C. No.10007/2025, as there was no change in circumstances, third application was dismissed as withdrawn on 18.06.2025 in M.Cr.C. No.20650/2025 and fourth application was also dismissed as withdrawn on 25.09.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.41545/2025.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63095 2 MCRC-54512-2025 2.

Learned counsel for the applicant while arguing the matter has submitted that the first application of the applicant was rejected on merits vide order dated 24.01.2025, the Court has not properly considered the averments made in the FIR.
He has further submitted that the applicant is merely an employee and one of the employee/co-accused has been granted bail by order dated 28.04.2025.
He has submitted that even the allegation regarding cash is also not believable looking to the chain of events available on record.

He has further submitted that even from the charge sheet,
there is no material available which indicates the active involvement of the present applicant and,
therefore, he prays that this application may be allowed as applicant is behind bars for more than one year.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and submits that as per the allegation made against the applicant, it is a gang working for defrauding and cheating people and they have extracted the amount by defrauding the complainant.
He has further submitted that earlier out of four applications, two applications are already decided on merits and those orders were not challenged in higher Court.
It is further submitted that still seven accused persons are absconding.

It is also contended that under the existing circumstances, if bail is granted to the applicant, there will be possibility that he will not cooperate in the trial and considering the material on record also, the involvement of the applicant is prima facie established and that such repeated bail application for fifth time without material change in the circumstances not required to be entertained.

4. I have considered the submissions made at the Bar and also NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63095 3 MCRC-54512-2025 considered the fact that earlier out of four bail applications, one application was rejected by giving detailed reasons and second application was also rejected by giving reasons as well as on the ground that there was no change in circumstances.
5.

Considering all these aspects and considering the fact that prima facie from the record,
involvement of the applicant in the crime in question cannot be ruled out.

Considering the fact that earlier also the Court has considered the bail applications on merits and rejected those bail applications, which were never challenged before the higher Court, such repeated application for fifth time without any substantial change in circumstances is not required to be entertained.
6. Accordingly, this fifth bail application is dismissed.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT) JUDGE b Javith Akthar @Javith S vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157432311/
